title: OrderBy Shuffle & Executor OOM
learningOutcome: Postmortem a failed nightly sorted export: explain why orderBy + coalesce(1) + collect_list under 512m executor memory OOMs
description: Acme needs one Parquet file of the day’s events, globally sorted by amount, for the warehouse loader. The job that does orderBy → coalesce(1) → collect_list(entire partition) on 2×512m executors OOMs on the real drop. This Side Quest is the postmortem: five reasoning questions on how that plan ran and why the executor died. Pass ≥ 80% (4 of 5).

problemStatement.overview: Incident: Acme’s nightly “one sorted Parquet file” events export failed with executor OOM on a 512m trail. Using the frozen FAILED History Server app, explain how orderBy + coalesce(1) + collect_list ran and why that heap was not enough.
symptoms: Warehouse loader requires one globally sorted events Parquet — not many part files.
The job (orderBy → coalesce(1) → collect_list “checksum” → write) works on a sample and dies on the full drop.
On-call sees FAILED / Java heap space and assumes “Spark is broken” instead of reading the plan.
yourTaskSteps: Read the frozen exhibit (session → orderBy → coalesce(1) → collect_list → write).
Open the frozen History Server app (status should be FAILED).
Answer five reasoning questions (no trivia from reading config lines).
Score at least 80% (4 of 5) to pass.
problemStatement.yourTask: Complete the postmortem quiz for the failed sorted-export job.
hints: Ask where the collect_list buffer lives for a coalesced partition — executor heap, not the driver.
A sample succeeding does not prove the plan fits 512m at full scale.
History should show Java heap space on the aggregation task — not a green job with an empty path.
